_note:
Slots for [brg_contact-routes]. NEW SECTION, Contact page, built from Expo SPEC-006. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`. Slot names are underscore-only. `text`/`textarea` defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`.

FOUR ROUTES, and the count is deliberate: it fits the 1 / 2x2 grid cleanly, and a switchboard with too many buttons is the thing a switchboard exists to prevent. Numbered slots are honest here for the same reason community-stats' are — the grid is a fixed design, not a feed.

A FIFTH is already foreseeable. Sean asked for phone links and no number exists yet, so a `Call us` card drops in as route_5 the day he supplies one; the fragment's CSS already handles an odd cell count, so that is an additive change with no layout work.

Two destinations are LIVE AND PROVEN today: route_1's general mailto and route_3's partnership mailto both work on community-partner. route_4 points at a live page. Only route_2 (press) is provisional, pending the Press page — if that page never ships, point it at a mailto.

Deliberately excluded per Expo, each for a reason: catering (belongs to the brand sites), guest complaints (a corporate address is the WRONG destination for a bad meal in Oceanside — slow, and the wrong team), and a phone number that rings an office nobody answers, which is worse than no number.

heading.label: Heading
heading.doc: Sits above the card grid. ~28 characters keeps it to one line.

route_1_label.label: Route 1 — label
route_1_label.doc: The teal link text. Short — it is a button, not a sentence.

route_1_href.label: Route 1 — link
route_1_href.doc: LIVE AND PROVEN — this mailto already works on community-partner.

route_1_text.label: Route 1 — one-liner
route_1_text.default: Anything that doesn't fit the boxes below.

route_2_href.label: Route 2 — link
route_2_href.doc: Points at the general inbox with a press subject line, the same pattern as route_3's proven partnership mailto. INTENDED DESTINATION is /press/#inquiries — switch it back the day the Press page ships (Expo SPEC-005). It is a mailto today because a slot default is LIVE COPY, so an aspirational default ships as a real defect: /press/ does not exist, and a dead link on a page whose whole job is routing people correctly is worse than a slightly generic destination.

route_2_text.default: Press kit, high-res imagery, interviews, or a comment on a story.

route_3_href.label: Route 3 — link
route_3_href.doc: LIVE AND PROVEN — the same mailto community-partner uses, subject line included.

route_4_href.label: Route 4 — link
route_4_href.doc: Points at the live careers page.

route_4_text.label: Route 4 — one-liner
route_4_text.doc: One line under the label. Write `&` as a literal ampersand.
route_4_text.default: Open roles across Board & Brew and Odie's.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.
